title: Add LRU+TTL eviction to CSV provider cache
description:
**MEMORY STABILITY**: CSV provider cache (providers/csv.py:68) grows without bounds. No size limit, no TTL expiry, no cleanup on mission change.

Key finding: Current memory estimation (200 bytes/position) underestimates by 70%. Actual usage is ~650 bytes/position. Long missions could consume 160+ MB in cache alone.

Solution: Create LRUTTLCache utility class and integrate into CSV provider:
- Size limit: 50 files
- TTL: 1 hour
- Thread-safe with RLock
- Statistics for diagnostics panel

Reference: `FINDINGS/results_deep_dive_C.md` for complete implementation including LRUTTLCache class code.
acceptance_criteria:

title: Implement safe GeoPackage backup with VACUUM INTO
description:
**DATA INTEGRITY RISK**: Current backup implementation uses `shutil.copy2()` on live GeoPackage files (utils/mission_storage.py:204, 249). This can produce inconsistent/corrupt backups when:
- QGIS layers have uncommitted edits
- SQLite has active transactions
- WAL journal mode is active

Solution: Replace with SQLite's `VACUUM INTO` (primary) or `connection.backup()` (fallback).

Files to modify:
- `utils/mission_storage.py` - Add `create_safe_snapshot()` function
- Update `sync_backup()` to use safe snapshot
- Update `create_archive()` to use temporary snapshot

Reference: `FINDINGS/results_deep_dive_B.md` and `FINDINGS/sqlite_backup_analysis.md` for complete implementation code.
acceptance_criteria:
- create_safe_snapshot() function with VACUUM INTO + fallback
- sync_backup() uses safe snapshot
- create_archive() creates temp snapshot before zipping
- No data loss during active tracking sessions
- Works on all supported QGIS versions

title: Review global vendor injection impact on other plugins
description:
**LOW PRIORITY STABILITY RISK**: sartracker.py forcefully rewrites `sys.path` (line 36) and purges `requests/urllib3/...` from `sys.modules` (line 128) at import time.

This can break other QGIS plugins that already imported `requests` or rely on different versions. During active rescue operations, other plugins might be in use (basemap, geocoding, device integrations).

Current approach attempts to ensure bundled vendor stack is used, but affects global interpreter.

Suggested mitigations:
- Only adjust sys.path locally around import calls
- Avoid global sys.modules purge
- Add guard to only adjust when requests not yet imported
- Document compatibility behavior in diagnostics panel

Reference: `FINDINGS/findings.md` Finding #1 for details.
acceptance_criteria:
- Impact assessment documented
- Decision on mitigation approach
- If changed: no regression in vendor imports
- If not changed: risk documented in diagnostics
